messages:
Mikaela (CS): Quick pocket guide I drafted for go-live handoffs — a tiny runbook focused on prefill/batching/streaming + renewal-signal capture. Link (internal): https://redwood.internal/runbooks/pocket-livehand
Mikaela (CS): TL;DR: soft-progressive-prefill, small batch windows for interactivity, streaming for UI flows, quick smoke telemetry + renewal-risk mapping :memo:
Andrew (SE): nice. can you drop a minimal client config so SEs can hand to customers? keeps onboarding friction low
Mikaela (CS): added a minimal snippet below you can paste to customers:
```json
{"prefill":true,"prefill_strategy":"soft_progressive","prefill_duration_s":30,"batch_window_ms":40,"max_batch_tokens":256,"stream":true,"client_keepalive_s":30}
```
Kai (Eng): perf notes: - warm-pool prewarm for top-5 prefixes reduces cold token p50 by ~30% - set kv-cache prefill for those prefixes with cache-ttl=600s - prefer progressive prefill so we ramp up without spiking GPUs
Sylvia (PM): can we attach a short mapping from telemetry -> renewal risk level for CS playbooks? e.g. low usage + rising latency -> risk medium, quality regressions -> high
Mikaela (CS): suggested mapping added: low (<50 active seats OR <10% baseline usage), medium (50–75% drop vs baseline OR latency >1.2x p50), high (quality regressions flagged by evals OR explicit negative NPS). also include recommended cadence per risk bucket.
Toni (CS): I'll own the 'customer checklist' to hand at kickoff. needs: sample prompt set, expected p95 latency, peak QPS, sample convo length, and an example traffic pattern file. I'll draft a 1-page handout. @Mikaela (CS)
Liam (Research): add an automated fallback policy: if eval-run (canary) reports >3 regressions on safety/accuracy on a rolling 1h window, route that customer's traffic to the higher-fidelity variant for 5–15 minutes and alert CS
Andrew (SE): troubleshooting snippet request: common "stuck stream" steps (client keepalive, check SSE disconnects, review server-side stream buffer). can you add a couple of CLI checks?
Mikaela (CS): added quick troubleshooting checks to the doc: `curl` to SSE endpoint, check `x-request-id` in logs, verify client heartbeat. small example:
```bash
# verify SSE stream open (returns events)
curl -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \ 
  https://api.redwood.ai/v1/streams/verify?model=xxx
```
Ops-bot: Deployment note: staging -> prod roll scheduled 2026-01-14T18:00Z by @deploy-bot :calendar:
Kai (Eng): also recommend default prefill jitter/backoff: base=200ms, jitter=0.25, cap=2s. keeps many tenants from synchronizing prefill bursts.
Mikaela (CS): feedback capture plan: short pulse survey 48h after go-live with 3 quick questions: accuracy (Likert), latency acceptable (Y/N + comment), any hallucinations observed (Y/N + example). store responses in ticket and tag account health.
Toni (CS): will include a link to the survey in onboarding email. also scheduling a 15m check-in 72h post-live for high-risk customers by default.
Liam (Research): small note on eval hooks: include a tiny eval set (10 prompts) that runs automatically 24–48h after go-live and whenever a model variant flips in routing. gives early signal on regressions.
Sylvia (PM): +1 on cadence and signals. add SLA expectations per tier in the playbook so customer-facing teams give consistent answers.
Andrew (SE): one more: example JSON for client traffic profile to give to SREs/eng when ramping:
```json
{"peak_qps":12,"avg_tokens_per_req":45,"interactive":true,"expected_session_length_s":120}
```
Mikaela (CS): great. I'm going to push this into playbooks as "Pocket Livehand Guide" and run a 20m sync with CS+SE next Tue to walk through handoff items. I'll capture action items in the doc.
Toni (CS): I'll draft the one-pager and share in #customer-success by EOD Fri :thumbsup:
Kai (Eng): will add the warm-pool prewarm job to the ops checklist and provide a short runbook for engineers.
Mikaela (CS): thanks all — if no objections, finalizing doc and scheduling sync. closing thread and moving actions into the shared doc. /end
